slots.description: Find the best photo for an anime portrait, from selfies and headshots to full-body images. Learn about lighting, resolution, poses and photo quality before ordering.
slots.intro: The best photo for an anime portrait gives an artist a clear view of your face, hair, expression and proportions. It does not need to be a professional studio image. A well-lit phone photo can work beautifully when the subject is sharp, unobstructed and facing the camera. For a custom anime portrait from photo, the source image is the artist’s visual reference—not a filter or automatic conversion. At Anime Cabinet, human artists hand-draw each portrait in your chosen visual language. You can choose from 24 anime and cartoon-inspired styles, receive a preview within 72 hours and request unlimited free revisions. The finished character is original to you, fan-art inspired rather than an impersonation of a copyrighted character.

[{"heading":"What is the best photo to use for a custom anime portrait?","body":"The best photo for a custom anime portrait is clear, well-lit and large enough for the artist to study important details. Choose an image where the subject is in focus, the face is not hidden by sunglasses or heavy shadows, and the hairline and jaw are easy to see. A relaxed expression, natural pose and uncluttered background also help.

You can send more than one reference if you want to combine details. For example, one image may show your preferred smile while another shows your hairstyle, glasses or outfit more clearly. Tell the artist which details matter most. This is especially useful when ordering a custom anime portrait canvas, because the composition may need to be planned around the final print shape.","heading":"What kind of photo works best for an anime-style portrait commission?","body":"For an anime-style portrait commission, use a photo that matches the result you want. A front-facing or three-quarter headshot is ideal for a traditional portrait. A side profile can work if you want a more dramatic character pose, but the nose, chin and cheek outline should remain visible. For action-inspired artwork, choose a photo with a readable pose and enough space around the body.

Avoid images that are heavily compressed, cropped through the hair or covered by strong filters. Beauty filters can remove features that make the finished portrait recognisably yours. Human artists can interpret imperfect source material, but accurate references give them more control over expression, likeness and costume details.","heading":"Should I use a close-up or full-body photo for an anime portrait?","body":"Use a close-up when the face is the main focus. A head-and-shoulders photo makes it easier to capture eye direction, eyebrows, hairstyle, skin tone and expression. It is usually the safest choice for a profile image, gift portrait or close crop.

Use a full-body photo when clothing, height, pose, footwear or a character concept is important. A full-body reference does not need to show every facial detail perfectly if you can also provide a separate headshot. For groups, send a high-resolution image with enough space between people, plus individual close-ups if faces are small. Your artist can then create a balanced group composition instead of enlarging an unclear face.","heading":"What resolution should a photo be for a custom anime portrait?","body":"There is no single mandatory resolution, but a larger original file gives an artist more useful information. As a practical guide, send the original camera or phone image rather than a screenshot or social-media download. A photo around 1,000 pixels wide can be workable for a single subject, while 2,000 pixels or more is preferable for a detailed print or a custom anime portrait canvas.

Do not enlarge a tiny image repeatedly, since artificial enlargement cannot restore missing facial detail. If your only reference is small, send it anyway and explain what must be preserved. The artist may be able to work from it, especially when supported by another photo, but very blurry details may need to be interpreted rather than copied precisely.","heading":"Can I use a casual selfie for an anime portrait commission?","body":"Yes. A casual selfie can be an excellent reference for a custom anime portrait commission online if it is sharp and evenly lit. Face a window or soft light source, clean the camera lens and hold the phone far enough away to avoid extreme wide-angle distortion. Keep your full head in frame, including the top of your hair and chin.

A selfie taken from very close range can make the nose or forehead look larger than usual. If possible, take a second photo from a little farther away at eye level. You do not need to pose formally: a genuine smile, favourite expression or everyday outfit can make the final original character feel more personal.","heading":"What lighting and background are best?","body":"Soft, even lighting is usually best. Daylight near a window works well when the light falls across the face rather than directly behind the subject. Avoid strong overhead lighting, coloured bulbs and bright backlighting, which can hide the eyes or change the apparent skin and hair colours. If you use flash, check that it has not created harsh reflections in glasses.

A simple background helps the artist separate the subject from the surroundings, but it is not essential. Tell us if you want a particular room, landscape or themed setting included. For a style inspired by [Ghibli-style artwork](/portraits/ghibli-style), [Demon Slayer](/portraits/demon-slayer) or another option in our collection, the artist can develop an original character composition rather than reproducing a copyrighted character exactly.","heading":"Can an artist create an anime portrait from an old or blurry photo?","body":"Sometimes, yes—but expectations should be realistic. An old photo may still provide valuable information about a person’s hairstyle, smile, clothing or overall pose. Send the highest-quality scan or original file you have, and include additional recent references where possible. Notes such as ‘keep the freckles,’ ‘use the hairstyle from photo two’ or ‘please match the blue jacket’ help resolve uncertainty.

A very blurry image may not support a precise likeness, especially for small eyes, jewellery or patterned clothing. During the hand-drawn process, you receive a preview within 72 hours to check the interpretation. Unlimited free revisions mean you can request changes before approving the artwork.","heading":"Photo tips for popular anime-inspired portrait requests","body":"Your photo does not have to show you dressed as a fictional hero. For a custom anime portrait Naruto request, for example, you can provide a normal portrait and describe the ninja-inspired mood, colours or setting you prefer. The same approach works for One Piece, Dragon Ball Z, Bleach, Jujutsu Kaisen and other fan-art-inspired directions. The result presents you as an original character in that visual language, not as a copyrighted character impersonation.

If you are comparing a custom anime portrait Etsy listing, a custom anime portrait free app or a professional custom anime portrait shop, check how the artwork is made and whether revisions are included. Automated filters may be quick, but they do not provide the same human composition, communication or hand-drawn refinement. Anime Cabinet lets you choose from 24 styles, review a real artist’s preview and refine the result without revision fees. Customers in Australia can order a custom anime portrait Australia-wide, with the same online process and preview timeline.","heading":"Before you upload: a simple checklist","body":"Before placing your order, choose the sharpest original image, check that the face and hair are visible, and remove heavy filters. Add a second reference for a different expression, outfit or pose when useful. Mention glasses, piercings, tattoos, freckles, pets, props and background preferences in your notes. If the portrait will be printed, tell the artist whether you prefer a close crop, portrait orientation or a wider composition.

The best photo for an anime portrait is ultimately the one that communicates you clearly. It can be a selfie, family snapshot or older photograph when the artist has enough information to work with. Upload your references to begin a hand-drawn custom portrait, then use the preview and unlimited free revisions to guide the final artwork."}]
